# Small O Notation

Small o notation, denoted as o(g(n)), defines an upper bound on the growth of a function f(n) that is _not_ asymptotically tight. In simpler terms, f(n) is o(g(n)) if, for any positive constant c, there exists a value nΓéÇ such that f(n) is strictly less than c\*g(n) for all n greater than nΓéÇ. This means that g(n) grows strictly faster than f(n) as n approaches infinity.
